Subject: SSQ follow-up: provenance and access controls (ClearHealth DPA)

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. The InfoSec team had two follow-ups on the SSQ where we need a little more granularity before we can close the DPA annex:

1) Provenance for PII-derived artifacts — we saw in the SSQ that you retain request traces for 30 days. Can you confirm which artifacts are considered "derivatives" (embeddings, logs, model outputs) and which are purged vs retained? We need a mapping per artifact type and retention period.

2) Access matrix and emergency access — can you provide a current access matrix diagram showing service accounts, human roles with PII access, and any out-of-band emergency/unlock procedures? We also want to know which roles require justification and JIT approval.

If you could attach a dataflow diagram that highlights where tokens/PII traverse and where redaction/obfuscation happens, that would be ideal. We can treat anything marked as confidential under our DPA.

Appreciate it — target is to get this back to procurement by EOD Monday.

—Alex
Security Engineer
ClearHealth

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SSQ follow-up: provenance and access controls (ClearHealth DPA)

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (Customer Success) and Neha (Privacy) for the attachments and a short narrative.

Quick answers up front:
- Derivative artifacts: embeddings and model output summaries are considered derivatives. Request-level telemetry (request id, timestamp, route) is retained 30 days by default; embeddings are retained 90 days for cache warming, unless the customer requests otherwise; model outputs are retained 30 days unless explicitly logged by the application. We can shorten retention on a per-account basis via an annex.
- Access controls: human access is RBAC-based. Only SRE-on-call and the Privacy team can request elevated access; approvals require two approvers (requestor's manager + privacy) for JIT. Emergency access (break-glass) is logged and requires retrospective audit within 24 hours.

Attaching a dataflow svg and an access matrix workbook — these are marked internal/controlled. Please note the Diagram highlights the KV cache boundary and tokenization/redaction step.

We'll follow with a short summary PDF mapping the SSQ question IDs to our responses. If you want a redlined DPA clause for retention, we can propose language.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Privacy & Policy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dataflow_v1.2.svg (diagram), access_matrix_20260514.xlsx (matrix)

Subject: Re: SSQ follow-up: provenance and access controls (ClearHealth DPA)

Irene / team — thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments. A couple of clarification requests after reviewing the flows: 

1) Embeddings retention: you mentioned 90 days for cache warming. Does the 90-day retention apply to customer-specific embeddings created from PII, or only to ephemeral system caches? If customer-specific, we will need an option to disable retention or reduce to 0 days.

2) Break-glass audit: can you provide a sample audit record or schema for the required fields (who, why, duration, approvers, and evidence link)? Our audit tooling will ingest it.

3) Cross-border note: I see the dataflow indicates optional routing to a eu region for dedicated customers. For our DPA we need the explicit default routing behavior for hosted accounts in the US. Please state if any signal or enterprise policy could trigger cross-border transit (e.g., model fallback to eu).

If you can paste short, copy-ready statements for each point, procurement can accept them to move the annex.

—Alex

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hurst <alex.hurst@clearhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SSQ follow-up: provenance and access controls (ClearHealth DPA)

Alex — answers below in copy-ready form. I've also exported a sample break-glass audit record as a schema snippet into the PDF attachment (ssq_response_summary.pdf). If you need a machine JSON example let me know and we can drop it into the Drive folder.

1) Embeddings retention (copy-ready text): 
"Customer-specific embeddings created from PII are treated as customer data. By default, Redwood retains customer-specific embeddings for up to 90 days to improve cache hit rates and reduce inference cost. Customers may opt out of embeddings retention or request a reduced retention window (including 0 days) via an annex to the DPA; changes are applied with no data rehydration from backups."

2) Break-glass audit (copy-ready text + schema summary):
"All emergency elevated-access events are recorded as an immutable audit event containing: event_id, target_resource, acting_principal (email), justification_text, approver_ids (manager and privacy), start_timestamp, end_timestamp, and evidence_link (URL to session recording/log bundle). Audit events are retained for 1 year by default and are exportable on request for compliance reviews."

(See ssq_response_summary.pdf for a downloadable CSV schema and an example record.)

3) Cross-border routing (copy-ready text):
"Hosted US accounts are routed to US-based inference endpoints by default. Cross-border routing (to EU or APAC endpoints) may occur only if a customer explicitly configures multi-region routing, or in rare fallback scenarios where US capacity is unavailable and the customer has elected permissive routing in their account settings. Redwood will not route customer data across borders for model fallback if the customer has set a region-lock in their account or if the DPA/annex prohibits cross-border transfer."

Next steps: Marissa will coordinate an annex template if you want the 0-day embeddings option. Neha is copied for legal/privacy signoff language. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if procurement prefers.

Thanks — Irene
